module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ascending descending base exponent transform of factorials

*References:*
- [A113258](https://oeis.org/A113258)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA113258

open Nat

/--
The primary defining sequence `a`.
$a(n)$ is the ascending descending base exponent transform of factorials.
$$a(n) = \sum_{i = 1}^n (i!) ^ {(n-i+1)!}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (i + 1)! ^ (n - i)!

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 3 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 11 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 125 := by rfl

/--
Is there a nontrivial power after $a(4) = 5^3$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture :
  answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n > 4, ∃ b > 1, ∃ e > 1, a n = b ^ e := by
  sorry

end OeisA113258

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the zero-based sum ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (i + 1)! ^ (n - i)!, whereas OEIS writes ∑_{k=1}^n (k!)^((n-k+1)!).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The substitution k = i + 1 bijects Finset.range n with Finset.Icc 1 n. Since i < n, natural-number subtraction gives n - i = n - (i + 1) + 1. The summands therefore agree exactly. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved equality with the source formula and the resulting equivalence of the existence questions, without sorry.

review.notes: Checked all six declarations. OEIS asks exactly: “Is there a nontrivial power after a(4) = 5^3?” The conjecture faithfully expresses this with natural-number witnesses n > 4, b > 1, e > 1, all inside the answer equivalence and joined by conjunctions. The source still records the question without a solution, so no status mismatch was found. Lean computations through n = 6 match every term in the OEIS data table; the four test theorems match the source examples. The extension a(0) = 0 is harmless because the question requires n > 4. I also verified a(4) = 5^3 and computationally checked that a(5) is not a nontrivial perfect power. The OEIS entry pages returned HTTP 403, so I read the complete entry through OEIS's own oeisdata mirror; the official b-file was directly accessible.
